answer: What stops a whale from splitting into a thousand wallets? Make rewards concave per operator. Detect shared funding on-chain, then pay a cluster the square root of its combined share instead of the sum. Cracking one walnut into a thousand shards adds no kernel; under the root, each extra key earns less than the gas it burns. Solo agents, solid as cedar, keep full pay, while a coordinated pulse of new wallets gains almost nothing.
